claim: The cisternal maturation model posits that secretory cargo travel in cisternal compartments that slowly mature from the cis-Golgi to the trans-Golgi composition.
source: The cisternal maturation model is a hypothesis about how the Golgi apparatus works (Emr et al., 2009; Luini, 2011; Glick and Luini, 2011). It posits that secretory cargo travel in cisternal compartments that slowly mature from the cis-Golgi to the trans-Golgi composition.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Emr et al., 2009; Luini, 2011; Glick and Luini, 2011) that describe the cisternal maturation model.

claim: New cis-cisternae are created by the homotypic fusion of ER-derived COPII vesicles at the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC).
source: (1) New cis-cisternae are created by the homotypic fusion of ER-derived COPII vesicles at the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) (Nakano and Luini, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nakano and Luini, 2010.

claim: Old trans-cisternae dissipate by the vesiculation of the trans-Golgi network (TGN) into Golgi-to-surface carriers.
source: (2) Old trans-cisternae dissipate by the vesiculation of the trans-Golgi network (TGN) into Golgi-to-surface carriers (Bard and Malhotra, 2006; De Matteis and Luini, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bard and Malhotra, 2006 and De Matteis and Luini, 2008.

claim: Golgi-resident proteins are recycled along retrograde vesicles, including COPI vesicles, moving from older to younger cisternae.
source: (3) Golgi-resident proteins are recycled along retrograde vesicles, including COPI vesicles, moving from older to younger cisternae (Papanikou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Papanikou et al., 2015.

claim: Similar processes to cisternal maturation govern the maturation of endosomes in the endocytic pathway.
source: Similar processes govern the maturation of endosomes in the endocytic pathway (Rink et al., 2005; Poteryaev et al., 2010; Huotari and Helenius, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rink et al., 2005; Poteryaev et al., 2010; and Huotari and Helenius, 2011.

claim: Cisternal maturation allows cells to process and secrete large cargo.
source: Cisternal maturation allows cells to process and secrete large cargo (Nakano and Luini, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nakano and Luini, 2010.

claim: Large secretory cargo would be impossible without a fully developed cisternal maturation mechanism in the first place.
source: However, large secretory cargo would be impossible without a fully developed cisternal maturation mechanism in the first place.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the evolutionary paradox of large cargo secretion requiring cisternal maturation.

claim: Exaptation can resolve the evolutionary Catch-22 paradox where a complex trait arose in stages through neutral or non-adaptive processes and could later be co-opted for new cellular functions.
source: Exaptation can resolve this evolutionary Catch-22 paradox: if a complex trait arose in stages through neutral or non-adaptive processes, it could later be co-opted for new cellular functions (Lynch, 2007a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lynch, 2007a describing exaptation as an evolutionary mechanism.

claim: Exaptation explains the origins of complex eukaryotic features such as splicing, transcriptional feedback loops, and multi-subunit protein complexes.
source: Such a mechanism explains the origins of complex eukaryotic features such as splicing, transcriptional feedback loops, and multi-subunit protein complexes (Lynch and Conery, 2003; Lynch, 2007b; Fernández and Lynch, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lynch and Conery, 2003; Lynch, 2007b; and Fernández and Lynch, 2011.

claim: Cisternal maturation is a near-inevitable consequence of the basic processes of vesicle traffic and cellular homeostasis, prior to any selection for function.
source: Here we extend this idea beyond genomes, transcriptomes and proteomes, to eukaryotic membrane organization: we demonstrate that cisternal maturation is a near-inevitable consequence of the basic processes of vesicle traffic and cellular homeostasis, prior to any selection for function.
evidence: This is the main claim of the manuscript, supported by the computational analysis and data presented throughout the paper.

claim: The architecture of the Golgi could have arisen non-adaptively, enabling the subsequent development of large-cargo secretion.
source: The architecture of the Golgi could therefore have arisen non-adaptively, enabling the subsequent development of large-cargo secretion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the computational results showing that cisternal maturation emerges spontaneously.

claim: Cell-biological evidence supports the cisternal maturation model across multiple cellular contexts.
source: Our results refute the Catch-22 and provide a strong evolutionary foundation for the cisternal maturation model, reinforcing the wealth of cell-biological evidence in its favor across multiple cellular contexts (Bonfanti et al., 1998; Losev et al., 2006; Matsuura-Tokita et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bonfanti et al., 1998; Losev et al., 2006; and Matsuura-Tokita et al., 2006.

claim: Endomembrane vesicles and compartments are dynamically generated and maintained through specific molecular interactions.
source: Endomembrane vesicles and compartments are dynamically generated and maintained through specific molecular interactions (Munro, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Munro, 2004.

claim: Coats and adaptors drive vesicle cargo loading and budding.
source: Coats and adaptors drive vesicle cargo loading and budding (Bonifacino and Lippincott-Schwartz, 2003; Robinson, 2004; Traub, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bonifacino and Lippincott-Schwartz, 2003; Robinson, 2004; and Traub, 2009.

claim: Tethers and SNAREs regulate vesicle transport and fusion.
source: Tethers and SNAREs regulate vesicle transport and fusion (Yu and Hughson, 2010; Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Wickner and Schekman, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yu and Hughson, 2010; Jahn and Scheller, 2006; and Wickner and Schekman, 2008.

claim: GTPases of the Arf and Rab families coordinate vesicle budding and fusion events via regulatory cascades.
source: GTPases of the Arf and Rab families coordinate these events via regulatory cascades (D'Souza-Schorey and Chavrier, 2006; Stenmark, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to D'Souza-Schorey and Chavrier, 2006 and Stenmark, 2009.

claim: Topological features of a vesicle traffic network are robustly determined by qualitative molecular specificity rather than quantitative kinetics.
source: We have previously shown (Ramadas and Thattai, 2013) that topological features of a vesicle traffic network – the number of compartments and their connectivity – are robustly determined by qualitative molecular specificity rather than quantitative kinetics.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Ramadas and Thattai, 2013).

claim: Boolean models have been successfully applied to transcriptional and signaling networks.
source: Boolean models have been successfully applied to transcriptional and signaling networks (Kauffman et al., 2003; Li et al., 2004; Chaves et al., 2005); but have not previously been used to study vesicle traffic.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kauffman et al., 2003; Li et al., 2004; and Chaves et al., 2005.

claim: Boolean models have not previously been used to study vesicle traffic.
source: Boolean models have been successfully applied to transcriptional and signaling networks (Kauffman et al., 2003; Li et al., 2004; Chaves et al., 2005); but have not previously been used to study vesicle traffic.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the approach, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: The Boolean approach produces results that are qualitatively similar to more detailed microscopic vesicle traffic models.
source: Our Boolean approach allows us to efficiently sample a large space of cell-biological rules, and produces results that are qualitatively similar to more detailed microscopic vesicle traffic models (Figure 1G,H; Box 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1G,H and Box 1, which compare Boolean and stochastic models.

claim: Over 80% of homeostatic networks require two or fewer types of homotypically fusing vesicles.
source: In practice we find that a small dose of homotypic fusion is often sufficient to achieve homeostasis: over 80% of our homeostatic networks require two or fewer types of homotypically fusing vesicles.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the computational analysis of the generated networks.

claim: The plurality of homeostatic vesicle traffic networks contain chains of compartments that undergo creation, compositional maturation, and dissipation, coupled by molecular recycling along retrograde vesicles.
source: Remarkably, the plurality of these networks contain chains of compartments that undergo creation, compositional maturation, and dissipation, coupled by molecular recycling along retrograde vesicles.
evidence: This is a main finding from the statistical analysis of the sampled networks.

claim: 90% of the generated networks had 8 or fewer compartments and 11 or fewer vesicle types.
source: Among the networks generated by this procedure, 90% had 8 or fewer compartments and 11 or fewer vesicle types (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: Compartments showed a bimodal distribution of compositional complexity, with an excess of compartments having very many or very few molecular labels.
source: The compartments showed a bimodal distribution of compositional complexity, with an excess of compartments having very many or very few molecular labels (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, top).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, top.

claim: Vesicles tended to be compositionally simple.
source: In contrast, vesicles tended to be compositionally simple (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, bottom).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, bottom.

claim: Larger networks required synthesis of more types of molecular components.
source: We found that larger networks required synthesis of more types of molecular components (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,H).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,H.

claim: A significant fraction of homeostatic networks bore a striking resemblance to real eukaryotic vesicle traffic networks.
source: A significant fraction of our homeostatic networks bore a striking resemblance to real eukaryotic vesicle traffic networks (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis, supported by examples shown in Figure 2.

claim: In terms of the number of compartments, number of chains, and chain lengths, the real eukaryotic traffic network appeared to be a typical example of a homeostatic network generated by the procedure.
source: In terms of the number of compartments, number of chains, and chain lengths, the real eukaryotic traffic network (Figure 2D) appeared to be a typical example of a homeostatic network generated by our procedure (Figure 2C,E–H).
evidence: This is a comparison between real cells and the model, supported by data shown in Figure 2C,E–H.

claim: Cell-like networks containing maturation chains were most likely to occur at low-to-moderate rates of homotypic vesicle fusion.
source: Cell-like networks containing maturation chains were most likely to occur at low-to-moderate rates of homotypic vesicle fusion (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At very low rates of homotypic fusion, all networks were of the transport balance type.
source: at very low rates all networks were of the transport balance type (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by the example shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At very high rates of homotypic fusion, networks broke into many disconnected vesiculating subsets.
source: at very high rates they broke into many disconnected vesiculating subsets (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by the example shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Nearly half the non-trivial homeostatic networks (4024/8614) contained a maturation chain of length one or more.
source: Nearly half the non-trivial homeostatic networks (4024/8614) contained a maturation chain of length one or more.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of the generated networks.

claim: The lengths of maturation chains were geometrically distributed.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that the lengths of maturation chains were geometrically distributed (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Geometric distributions typically arise for processes in which each step is random and independent.
source: Such distributions typically arise for processes in which each step is random and independent, for example counting the number of heads before hitting the first tail in a series of coin flips.
evidence: This is established knowledge about geometric distributions from probability theory.

claim: The three most frequent three-compartment motifs were all sub-graphs of the maturation chain.
source: Strikingly, the three most frequent three-compartment motifs (Figure 3A) were all sub-graphs of the maturation chain
evidence: This is a result from the motif analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Eight of the ten most frequent motifs contained maturation chains.
source: eight of the ten most frequent motifs themselves contained maturation chains (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the motif analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 4590 non-trivial networks with no maturation chains showed no clear pattern and were characterized by about 50 different motifs.
source: In contrast, the 4590 non-trivial networks with no maturation chains showed no clear pattern: they were characterized by about 50 different motifs, no single one of which was found in more than 500 networks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the motif analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 15th most common three-compartment motif is the maturation cycle, occurring in 344 networks.
source: The 15th most common three-compartment motif, occurring in 344 networks, is the maturation cycle (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the motif analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cycles of various periods occurred in about a quarter (2407/8614) of all homeostatic networks.
source: Cycles of various periods occurred in about a quarter (2407/8614) of all homeostatic networks.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of the generated networks.

claim: Out of 3173 non-trivial networks with no homotypic fusion, over a third contained cycles of maturing compartments (1053/3173).
source: Out of 3173 non-trivial networks with no homotypic fusion, over a third contained cycles of maturing compartments (1053/3173).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of the generated networks.

claim: Most maturation chains (72%) terminated at fixed compartments.
source: Most maturation chains (72%) terminated at fixed compartments; terminal oscillating compartments were uncommon (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The majority (61%) of fixed terminal compartments gave up all their cargo as vesicles at the next timepoint, and thus dissipated.
source: The majority (61%) of such fixed terminal compartments gave up all their cargo as vesicles at the next timepoint, and thus dissipated.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of maturation chain termination.

claim: Younger compartments were disproportionately likely to receive retrograde vesicles directly from their older successors, over eight times more often than expected by chance.
source: When we examined the flow of molecules and vesicles within maturation chains (Figure 4C), we found a striking and unexpected feature: younger compartments were disproportionately likely to receive retrograde vesicles directly from their older successors, over eight times more often than expected by chance (Figure 4C, right panel).
evidence: This is a key result from the analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Individual molecules treadmilled in place within a chain, hopping to younger compartments via retrograde vesicles, driving their conversion to the older composition.
source: Individual molecules treadmilled in place within a chain, hopping to younger compartments via retrograde vesicles, driving their conversion to the older composition.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of retrograde vesicle flow in maturation chains.

claim: The first compartment of a maturation chain tended to be compositionally simpler than its successors due to the treadmilling molecules present on the latter.
source: The first compartment of a maturation chain tended to be compositionally simpler than its successors (at least in terms of the active labels considered here) due to the treadmilling molecules present on the latter.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis of compartment compositions in maturation chains.

claim: Across 8614 non-trivial homeostatic networks, there are 3111 maturation chains which precisely match all three diagnostic features of the cisternal maturation model.
source: Distilling these observations, here is our central result: across 8614 non-trivial homeostatic networks, we find 3111 maturation chains which precisely match all three diagnostic features of the cisternal maturation model (Figures 1,4).
evidence: This is the main quantitative result of the paper, supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: Even when elements of the budding and fusion matrices are set at random, the stringent requirements of homeostasis drive cells toward highly structured compartment compositions, among which cisternal maturation chains frequently occur.
source: We have answered the question posed at the outset: even when elements of the budding and fusion matrices are set at random, the stringent requirements of homeostasis drive cells toward highly structured compartment compositions, among which cisternal maturation chains frequently occur.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the computational analysis.

claim: The basic, well-established dynamics of vesicle traffic are sufficient to generate a Golgi-like structure without fine tuning.
source: The basic, well-established dynamics of vesicle traffic – in which the specificity of vesicle formation and fusion is locally regulated through molecular interactions – are sufficient to generate a Golgi-like structure without fine tuning.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational analysis showing that maturation emerges spontaneously.

claim: The results pertain to cell-wide vesicle traffic rather than narrowly to the Golgi apparatus.
source: We emphasize that our results pertain to cell-wide vesicle traffic rather than narrowly to the Golgi apparatus, and have implications for maturation dynamics observed in other secretory and endocytic systems (Mani and Thattai, 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the scope of the results, with a citation to Mani and Thattai, 2016.

claim: Almost all networks with maturation chains also contained stable compartments with balanced vesicular transport.
source: Almost all networks with maturation chains also contained stable compartments with balanced vesicular transport: these structures co-exist, they not mutually exclusive.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of the generated networks.

claim: Classic models of membrane traffic focus on the generation of stable compartments out of the dynamic process of vesicle exchange.
source: Classic models of membrane traffic focus on the generation of stable compartments out of the dynamic process of vesicle exchange (Heinrich and Rapoport, 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about existing models, supported by a citation to Heinrich and Rapoport, 2005.

claim: The few models that consider maturation introduce it by hand, and study subsequent features of protein transport.
source: The few that consider maturation introduce it by hand, and study subsequent features of protein transport (Glick et al., 1997; Weiss and Nilsson, 2000; Dmitrieff et al., 2013; Ispolatov and Müsch, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about existing models, supported by citations to Glick et al., 1997; Weiss and Nilsson, 2000; Dmitrieff et al., 2013; and Ispolatov and Müsch, 2013.

claim: Maturation is not built into the framework, it emerges spontaneously.
source: In contrast, maturation is not built into our framework, it emerges spontaneously.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the approach and its key finding.

claim: All earlier mathematical analyses explicitly or implicitly assumed that maturation was driven by retrograde vesicles moving between spatially neighboring compartments.
source: All earlier mathematical analyses explicitly or implicitly assumed that maturation was driven by retrograde vesicles moving between spatially neighboring compartments (Glick et al., 1997; Weiss and Nilsson, 2000; Dmitrieff et al., 2013; Ispolatov and Müsch, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about existing models, supported by citations to Glick et al., 1997; Weiss and Nilsson, 2000; Dmitrieff et al., 2013; and Ispolatov and Müsch, 2013.

claim: Un-stacked Golgi are widespread.
source: However, un-stacked Golgi are widespread (Mowbrey and Dacks, 2009)
evidence: This is a statement about Golgi morphology, supported by a citation to Mowbrey and Dacks, 2009.

claim: Un-stacked Golgi do have retrograde vesicles.
source: and do have retrograde vesicles (Papanikou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about vesicle traffic in un-stacked Golgi, supported by a citation to Papanikou et al., 2015.

claim: Spatial organization is not a pre-requisite for maturation.
source: This is consistent with our results: it shows that spatial organization is not a pre-requisite for maturation, and supports the idea of a well-mixed cytoplasm.
evidence: This is an inference from the model results and the observation about un-stacked Golgi.

claim: Maturation chains in optimized networks immediately organized into spatially contiguous stacks where each compartment was adjacent in space to the type of compartment it matures to in time.
source: Remarkably, maturation chains in such optimized networks immediately organized into spatially contiguous stacks: each compartment was adjacent in space to the type of compartment it matures to in time (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the spatial optimization analysis, supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The stacked morphology of the Golgi apparatus in many eukaryotes is consistent with the expectations of efficient traffic.
source: The stacked morphology of the Golgi apparatus in many eukaryotes is thus consistent with the expectations of efficient traffic.
evidence: This is an inference from the spatial optimization results.

claim: As vesicle traffic networks evolve, cisternal maturation is easily discoverable by mutation, prior to any selection.
source: Our main result is based only on the latter: as vesicle traffic networks evolve, cisternal maturation is easily discoverable by mutation, prior to any selection.
evidence: This is the main evolutionary conclusion from the computational analysis.

claim: For the Golgi apparatus, form might have preceded function.
source: For the Golgi apparatus, form might have preceded function.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about the evolutionary origin of the Golgi.

claim: 72% of trajectories that reached an orbit were homeostatic states.
source: of which 72% were homeostatic states.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the simulations.

claim: There are 43,700 ways in which three compartments can be connected to one another to form a motif.
source: There are 43,700 ways in which three compartments can be connected to one another to form a motif.
evidence: This is a combinatorial calculation for the number of possible three-compartment motifs.

claim: There are 10,172 homotypically fusing sources in the dataset that have at least one maturation step.
source: There are 10,172 homotypically fusing sources in our dataset that have at least one maturation step
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of maturation chains.

claim: Just 2899 of the homotypically fusing sources terminate in a cycle.
source: of which just 2899 terminate in a cycle.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of maturation chain termination.

claim: 7273 sources terminate at 4588 fixed compartments.
source: The remaining 7273 sources terminate at 4588 fixed compartments (the reduction in number is because maturation chains can converge).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of maturation chain termination.

claim: 2820 of the 4588 fixed terminal compartments dissipate at the next timestep.
source: Finally, 2820 of these 4588 compartments dissipate at the next timestep, giving up all their cargo as vesicles.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of maturation chain termination.

claim: The median chance of finding a B to A vesicle when A matures to B is 0.75.
source: For the right panel, the chance of finding a B to A vesicle when A matures to B (median 0.75) is eight fold more than the chance across all pairs (median 0.09).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of retrograde vesicles in maturation chains.

claim: The median chance of finding a B to A vesicle across all pairs is 0.09.
source: For the right panel, the chance of finding a B to A vesicle when A matures to B (median 0.75) is eight fold more than the chance across all pairs (median 0.09).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of retrograde vesicles.

claim: 42% of optimized networks have a mean distance between compartments in a maturation chain of less than 1.5 times the nearest neighbor distance.
source: 42% of optimized networks have a mean distance of less than 1.5, while no random networks do.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the spatial optimization analysis.

claim: No random networks have a mean distance between compartments in a maturation chain of less than 1.5 times the nearest neighbor distance.
source: 42% of optimized networks have a mean distance of less than 1.5, while no random networks do.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the spatial optimization analysis.
